transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-05 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Javier Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Solaris Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (CTO), Sanjay Patel (SRE), Nora Li (Product)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Solaris' target to go from prototype to first production calls. They've done small POCs on other providers; evaluating hosted (fast TTFT) vs dedicated/reserved capacity (predictable latency/cost) vs private/VPC for compliance. Looking for free credits to accelerate integration and a clear path to demo latency numbers in their environment.

Topics discussed: time-to-first-token (TTFT) and quickstart flow, free credits and billing estimate, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, security/KMS and VPC constraints, rollout & success criteria for a pilot, next steps and artifacts to share.

Transcript:
[00:00] Javier: hey everyone thanks for joining, hi i'm javier from Redwood, with priya from our se team. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: hey thanks, we're good, quick morning here — appreciate you fitting this in.
[00:15] Liam: yeah thanks, short preface — we're evaluating options for embedding search and a chat assistant into our checkout experience, need low latency and tight cost control.
[00:26] Priya: great, that's helpful. can you share the rough qps and token sizes you're expecting? just to ballpark when we'd talk hosted vs dedicated.
[00:34] Maya: current prototype, about 6–10 qps hitting the assistant with average prompts ~120 tokens and responses about 300 tokens; spikes during sales events might go to 40 qps.
[00:45] Javier: perfect. so time-to-first-token — do you mean latency from request to first token streamed back, or time to get a working API key and a demo up and running?
[00:53] Nora: both, really. product needs to demo a working flow to stakeholders in 2 weeks; engineering needs to understand the path to production in 8–12 weeks.
[01:05] Priya: ok that's reasonable. for a demo we can get you an API key and sample app running in hours with our hosted API, and we'll allocate trial credits so you can hit realistic token volumes. the hosted is fastest TTFT.
[01:16] Sanjay: regarding hosted — can you confirm data retention and whether logs leave our VPC? we can't have raw customer PII stored externally.
[01:24] Javier: good call — our hosted product has opt-in data retention controls. by default telemetry that's used for platform ops is kept for X days, but we can disable training/usage retention for your account; for strict requirements you'd look at our Dedicated or Private options.
[01:36] Liam: can you explain the difference operationally? like what changes when we pick Dedicated vs Private?
[01:42] Priya: sure. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput and isolation at the tenancy level, but still managed by Redwood. Private gives you a customer-controlled plane: VPC peering or on-prem where you control the network and key management (KMS/HSM). Dedicated is quicker to stand up and has SLA-backed latency targets; Private is for when you need full network isolation or regulatory controls.
[02:02] Maya: what's the typical latency delta? we care about 95th percentile under burst.
[02:07] Priya: in many e‑com workloads, hosted can be ~80–150ms first-token for smaller models under low QPS, but it depends on model choice and batching. Dedicated tuned for a given sequence length mix gets you tighter 95th percentiles — often reducing tail by 20–40ms in our experience. Private performance is similar to Dedicated when deployed on comparable hardware, but it depends on your infra.
[02:29] Liam: are there auto-fallbacks if my dedicated capacity is saturated? we want graceful degradation rather than timeouts.
[02:35] Javier: yes — smart routing can fallback to an equivalent hosted model variant if your Dedicated pool is fully utilized; we can set policies: prioritize latency or cost.
[02:44] Sanjay: firewall question — we run egress only via proxy, can we restrict outbound traffic?
[02:49] Priya: yes, for Private we can work with your network team to allow only necessary endpoints. for Dedicated there's also options for VPC peering and IP allowlists.
[02:58] Nora: on the credits — what's realistic for us to prove production fit? we want to generate a couple million tokens to simulate a weekend sales blast.
[03:06] Javier: we typically offer a tailored free credit bundle depending on scope; for a weekend-scale test we'd put you in the 50k–200k USD equivalent token range depending on model. we'll propose a specific allocation in the follow-up.
[03:18] Maya: that helps. and pricing — is it purely usage-based for Hosted? how does Dedicated billing look?
[03:24] Javier: Hosted is usage-based per token and embeddings. Dedicated is a reserved commit for capacity (monthly/annual) plus a nominal per-token or overage structure. The tradeoff is predictability and lower unit costs at scale.
[03:36] Liam: ok. security — SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs? we have auditors asking for those.
[03:43] Priya: we have SOC 2 Type II, SAML/SSO integrations, RBAC in the console, and detailed audit logging with export options; we'll send the security package and the SOC 2 report link.
[03:54] Sanjay: KMS — we need customer-managed keys. does Private support HSMs?
[03:58] Priya: yes, Private supports customer KMS/HSM for key material. Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest keys; for full HSM-backed workflows Private or on-prem is recommended.
[04:08] Maya: earlier you mentioned model variants for fallback. is there an easy way to pin a version and do canary rollouts?
[04:13] Javier: yep — our rollout features let you pin model versions per route and do gradual percentage rollouts with automatic fallback and health checks. you can also set per-customer or per-route quotas.
[04:24] Liam: about model choice—our prototype used a 7B open model quantized to int8. does Redwood host quantized models or do we bring our own?
[04:31] Priya: both. we host a catalog of vetted open models with verified perf profiles and also support bringing your own model artifacts. for BYOM there are packaging/quantization guidelines.
[04:40] Maya: great, can you provide a sample perf profile for a 7B int8 model with our token mix?
[04:45] Priya: yes, i'll run a short matrix (hosted vs dedicated) for your prompt/response size and share numbers — i'll include simulated burst scenarios.
[04:52] Liam: what about batching and caching — we'd like to reduce cost without sacrificing latency.
[04:56] Priya: caching for common prefixes and KV cache reuse for chat contexts are supported; intelligent batching can be tuned — for checkout recommendations, small constant batching windows help reduce cost while keeping latency under SLOs.
[05:10] Maya: do you have any guardrails for hallucinations or deterministic outputs? we need controlled outputs for purchase instructions.
[05:16] Javier: yes — structured output support, response schemas and function/tool calling help constrain outputs. we also have eval tooling to monitor regressions against prompt sets.
[05:26] Nora: stakeholder timeline — we need a small demo for execs in two weeks. is that tight?
[05:31] Javier: doable. Hosted + quickstart credits gets you there fastest. We'll provide a sample React widget and step-by-step.
[05:39] Liam: is there an SDK or just REST?
[05:41] Priya: we have REST plus SDKs (node, python) and examples for streaming and function calling.
[05:46] Sanjay: compliance note — can we get a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and terms for GDPR/data residency?
[05:52] Javier: yes, we'll attach our DPA and note residency options — Dedicated or Private are better if you need an EU-only footprint.
[06:00] Maya: ok very clear. two technical quick asks: 1) sample hosted latency under our token mix, 2) a simple dedicated sizing rec for 40 qps bursts.
[06:09] Priya: got it. we'll produce the two-page quickstart perf note and a dedicated sizing ballpark — with GPUs, expected tokens/sec, and cost estimate.
[06:18] Liam: one more — what visibility will our ops team get into request-level costs and token breakdowns?
[06:23] Javier: console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards and tracing hooks and you can export CSVs to your BI.
[06:33] Sanjay: if we go Dedicated, what's the usual lead time to bring it up?
[06:36] Priya: setup for Dedicated can be weeks (2–6) depending on capacity and contract; Private on a customer's VPC can take longer because of network/security signoffs. For the demo we recommend Hosted.
[06:48] Maya: what's the common pilot length you see? 4–8 weeks?
[06:52] Javier: 4–8 weeks is common — validate correctness and tail latency during a couple of peak events, then decide on a dedicated pilot or scale hosted.
[07:00] Liam: competitors — we've run tests with OpenAI but had cost surprises on spikes. are routing/cost controls part of Redwood?
[07:07] Priya: yes — routing policies can prefer cheaper variants unless latency SLOs are violated; we also provide quantization and caching suggestions to control unit economics.
[07:16] (brief cross-talk)
[07:20] Nora: ok — from a product perspective we'd like a small scoped pilot that shows both the UX and operational metrics.
[07:25] Javier: understood. proposed pilot: 4 weeks, hosted with 100k USD-equivalent credits, perf benchmark + 1 simulated sales spike, and acceptance criteria: 95th < target latency (you'll give number), error rate < 0.5%.
[07:36] Maya: sounds right, need to confirm the actual latency target internally but that format makes sense.
[07:41] Javier: perfect. i'll follow up with a playbook and the credits proposal.
[07:46] Liam: two practical things — can we get IP allowlist IP addresses and a swagger sample for quick integration?
[07:52] Priya: yes on both. i'll include API endpoints, sample curl and SDK snippet in the follow-up.
[07:59] Sanjay: any logs you can stream to our datadog?
[08:03] Priya: we can forward audit logs and metrics to your observability stream; we'll include common Grafana/Datadog dashboards.
[08:12] (phone buzz)
[08:16] Maya: apologies, just a note — our compliance folks will request the SOC report and DPA, again request to disable retention for test org.
[08:24] Javier: understood, we'll provide SOC 2 artifact and DPA and set retention flags off for your trial org.
[08:30] Nora: last Q — any recommended prompt engineering guardrails for checkout flows?
[08:36] Priya: use schema enforcement and function-calling for structured responses, short system prompts that assert constraints, and a post-process validation layer to catch malformed outputs. we can share playbook examples.
[08:47] Maya: thanks. this was helpful.
[08:50] Javier: thanks everyone — we'll send the playbook, credits, SOC2/DPA, and a perf matrix. any other blockers?
[08:58] Liam: none from me.
[09:00] Sanjay: nope.
[09:02] Nora: all good.
[09:05] Javier: great — next step i'll email artifacts and we'll target the perf demo week of the 16th. thanks all.

Recap (auto):

- Solaris to provide: latency SLO (95th), VPC/network constraints, and sample prompts for evaluation.
